subtopics.title: The Logic of Growth on Growth

questions.question: What is the main difference between simple and compound growth?
options: Simple growth only gives interest on the original amount; compound growth gives interest on the original amount plus previous interest.
Compound growth only gives interest on the original amount; simple growth gives interest on the original amount plus previous interest.
They both give the same amount of money at the end.
Compound growth means you get less money each year.

questions.question: If you calculate 10% of R2 000, what decimal should you multiply R2 000 by?
In the context of compound growth, what does 'growth on top of growth' mean?
options: You plant new seeds every single year from scratch.
Your interest starts earning its own interest.
The bank gives you double the interest rate.

questions.question: You invest R4 000 at 5% per annum. How much interest do you earn in Year 1?
After earning R200 interest on a R4 000 investment in Year 1, what is the new total in your bank account?
How do you turn a 7% interest rate into a decimal for calculation?
If your total at the end of Year 1 is R4 200 and the interest rate is 5% p.a. compound interest, what amount do you calculate the Year 2 interest on?
At the start of Year 2 you have R4 200. The interest rate is 5%. What is the interest earned in Year 2?
Why is the interest in Year 2 (R210) higher than the interest in Year 1 (R200)?
options: Because the bank made a mistake.
Because the interest rate went up.
Because you are calculating 5% on a larger amount (R4 200 instead of R4 000).
Because 5% of R4 200 is less than 5% of R4 000.

questions.question: In the formula A = P(1 + i)^n, what does the 'P' stand for?
If you invest R10 000 at 6% p.a. compounded annually for 5 years, how do you substitute this into the formula?
What is the final answer for A = 10000(1 + 0,06)^5, rounded to two decimal places?
